title_en: Shenyin Wanguo Securities Co., Ltd. v. Shanghai Guohong Real Estate Co., Ltd. — dispute over property ownership
ruling_gist_en: 1. The nominee holding or entrustment of shares, that is, the anonymous holding of legal person shares in the usual sense. The anonymous holding of legal person shares involves an actual contributor and a nominal holder, and both parties should enter into a corresponding agreement to determine their relationship, thereby negating the shareholder rights of the nominal shareholder. Where one party is originally the owner of the legal person shares, and the other party obtains ownership of the legal person shares through a compensated transfer, and the agreement entered into by the parties is a legal person share transfer agreement that specifies the transfer consideration and the transfer of ownership, such a situation does not constitute nominee shareholding or entrustment; it can be determined that the parties transferred the ownership of the legal person shares through a sale. Even if the transferee has not paid any consideration, the transferor has already lost ownership of the disputed legal person shares and can only claim corresponding creditor's rights under the transfer agreement.
